title: Gradient descent and the learning rate
subtitle: Watch x<sub>k+1</sub> = x<sub>k</sub> − η f′(x<sub>k</sub>) converge, oscillate or blow up on a quadratic.

intro.idea: Gradient descent minimizes a function by repeatedly stepping against its slope: x<sub>k+1</sub> = x<sub>k</sub> − η f′(x<sub>k</sub>). On the quadratic f(x) = ½ a x<sup>2</sup> the slope is a x, so every step multiplies x by the same factor r = 1 − η a.
intro.why: The learning rate η is the most important knob when training models. Too small wastes time, too large makes training diverge. The quadratic shows exactly where the boundary is: |1 − η a| < 1, i.e. 0 < η < 2/a.

symbols.meaning: factor multiplying x at each step

visuals.title: Path on the loss curve
visuals.caption: Orange dots are the iterates x<sub>0</sub>, x<sub>1</sub>, …; the line joins them in order.

explorations.title: Small steps converge slowly
explorations.change: Press Try it, then raise η towards 1.
explorations.observe: With η = 0.1, x shrinks by 10% per step and is still ≈ 1.046 after 10 steps. At η = 1/a = 1 it reaches 0 in one step.
explorations.why: x<sub>k</sub> = (1 − η a)<sup>k</sup> x<sub>0</sub>; the closer r is to 0 the faster the error shrinks.

explorations.title: Too large a step diverges
explorations.observe: The iterates jump from side to side and grow; |r| = 1.1 > 1.
explorations.why: Each step overshoots the minimum by more than it started. The clean threshold 2/a holds for a quadratic; real losses have varying curvature, so it is only a local guide.

limitations: No noise: this is full-batch gradient descent, not SGD.
